about: BOLO 51's standing audit rows. Every GAP and PARTIAL row from BORESIGHT 64 (ruled 9/23, Call 3). audit.py prints the open ones; close one with audit.py close <id> <note>.

rows.practice: Separate exploration from implementation with plan mode
rows.gap: The separation is real but implicit in formation order, not an explicit approve-before-edit gate Chief can invoke on demand outside a formation.
rows.fix: None needed for formation work; for ad-hoc edits outside a named skill, Chief can still just say "plan only" as a habit.

rows.gap: Session-start context comes only from the digest hook and MEMORY.md; there is no short, checked-in file naming code style, testing, or workflow rules for this repo.
rows.fix: Write a short root CLAUDE.md pointing at SOP.md §1 and the skill list — a pointer file, not a duplicate of SOP.

rows.gap: The allowlist is real but thin — the routine commands this repo actually runs (python scripts, git status/diff, bash tool calls under _tools/) aren't on it, so most turns still prompt.
rows.fix: Run the fewer-permission-prompts skill against a week of transcripts and add the read-only commands it surfaces to `.claude/settings.local.json`.

rows.practice: Use CLI tools like gh for external services
rows.gap: The repo is public and commits happen every turn, but there is no path from a local autosave to an issue or PR — gh is simply unused.
rows.fix: Only worth doing when a PR-based workflow is actually wanted; otherwise leave as-is since autocommit-only fits the private-cadence, deliberate-push model.

rows.practice: Connect MCP servers for external integrations
rows.gap: Anything an MCP server would give (structured DB access, ticketing) is instead done by hand-rolled scripts per formation; no integration is missing that's currently blocking work.
rows.fix: Leave alone until a specific external service (e.g. a shared doc or ticket tracker) is named as needed.

rows.gap: If a specialist or the main line drifts mid-turn, there's no documented habit of using Esc/rewind to back out cleanly — the fallback is finish-then-fix.
rows.fix: None needed as a build; this is an interactive habit, not a repo artifact — just use Esc/Esc+Esc live.

rows.gap: The hook plumbing supports /clear; whether Chief actually clears between unrelated asks (vs. one long thread) isn't established by anything in command.md.
rows.fix: State it as a named habit in SOP §1 next to the four-step vocabulary — costs nothing to write, per ruling 3 this folds into BOLO 51 not a new section.

rows.gap: Chief is known to run two sessions at once against the same working tree; without worktree isolation those sessions can collide on the same files with no structural guard, only session-id discipline.
rows.fix: Adopt `--worktree` for the second concurrent session, or at minimum document the same-tree risk in SOP so it's a known tradeoff, not a blind spot.

rows.practice: Use PreToolUse hooks to validate commands
rows.gap: Nothing can deterministically block a tool call before it runs — e.g. the no-unasked-probing rule [C3] is enforced only by habit, not by a hook that could refuse the scan.
rows.fix: Write one PreToolUse hook that blocks process/network/log-scanning Bash patterns unless the order names the box — gives C3's memory rule real teeth.

rows.gap: A malformed JSON board or a script with a syntax error could land without any automatic check running right after the edit.
rows.fix: Low priority: this repo's own RANGE reviewer scripts already catch board-shape errors at the fan-in [C52]; a PostToolUse formatter would mostly help the python utilities.

rows.practice: Use Stop hooks as deterministic gates
rows.gap: The one Stop hook that runs on every turn is explicitly not a verification gate; if it were, an autosave failure would incorrectly block the session, so this is a deliberate tradeoff rather than an oversight.
rows.fix: No change recommended — keeping Stop non-blocking is the right call given autocommit's job; verification correctly lives in the reviewer scripts instead.

rows.gap: Any judgment-call enforcement (e.g. "is this a probing scan?") currently has no hook path at all, deterministic or prompt-based — it's pure habit [C46].
rows.fix: Not urgent — script-based PreToolUse coverage (see B2) would catch the sharpest cases more cheaply than a prompt-based hook.

rows.practice: Use agent-based hooks for complex validation
rows.gap: There's no hook-triggered agent validation step; the formation doctrine's own rule against agent-based checking (never a checker agent) [C15] makes this an intentional non-fit, not an oversight.
rows.fix: None recommended — conflicts with the ruled doctrine that RANGE is always a script.

rows.practice: Hook events include SessionStart and SessionEnd
rows.gap: Session open is automated; session close still depends on Chief saying "Oscar Mike" and the skill running by hand [C25], not a SessionEnd hook that fires no matter how the session ends.
rows.fix: A SessionEnd hook that at minimum checks for an un-flushed Ready Rack note or dirty tree would catch a session that ends without an Oscar Mike.

rows.practice: Hook events include UserPromptSubmit and Stop
rows.gap: Nothing can inspect or gate an incoming prompt before Claude processes it — e.g. auto-detecting a proword or garble before the turn starts has to happen in-context instead.
rows.fix: Only worth adding if a specific per-prompt check is named; no current need is blocked by its absence.

rows.practice: Hook events include PreToolUse and PostToolUse
rows.gap: Same underlying gap as B2/B3 — no tool-call-level hook exists at all.
rows.fix: See B2's fix; one PreToolUse hook covers the highest-value case (no-unasked-probing enforcement).

rows.practice: Hook events include FileChanged and ConfigChange
rows.gap: A change to `.claude/settings.local.json` or a board JSON mid-session triggers nothing automatically.
rows.fix: Low value here — boards are only ever changed by scripts at defined formation steps, not edited live outside that flow.

rows.gap: Nothing in command.md shows a deliberate token budget being tracked for any agent description — it's small because the format is small, not because a limit is enforced.
rows.fix: No action needed while skill files stay this size; revisit only if a SKILL.md grows past a few KB.

rows.practice: Enforce tool restrictions with tools field
rows.gap: A PS or MS specialist could technically call any tool available to the Agent type it runs under; the "read nothing else" boundary is convention, not a config-enforced restriction.
rows.fix: Define named `.claude/agents/` files per crew grade (PS/MS) with an explicit `tools:` allowlist matching what each formation actually needs.

rows.gap: A PS/MS specialist doing pure fetch-and-write work still prompts (or auto-accepts) at the session's default rather than a mode scoped to its narrow, disjoint job.
rows.fix: Set `acceptEdits` on read-only-input specialists that only ever write one named file, once named `.claude/agents/` definitions exist (see C3).

rows.gap: A specialist that mis-writes has no structural containment — the fixed-output-contract convention [C38] is the only guard, not filesystem isolation.
rows.fix: Low priority given the fixed-output-contract discipline already limits blast radius to one named file per specialist.

rows.gap: A PS/MS that runs the same kind of extraction repeatedly (e.g. EXTRACT-k in collect) starts cold every time — no accumulated pattern knowledge carries between runs.
rows.fix: Not worth adding while specialists stay narrow and one-shot by design; revisit only if a specialist role becomes a recurring, evolving job.

rows.gap: Same root cause as B2/B9 — no PreToolUse hook exists to scope, whether at session or subagent level.
rows.fix: Covered by B2's fix; a subagent-scoped variant is a follow-on once the session-level hook exists.

rows.gap: There's nothing to organize because named subagent files were never created — crew-grade identity lives in SOP prose, not in a `name:` field on a checked-in file.
rows.fix: Only needed if named `.claude/agents/` definitions get created (see C3, C5); until then there's nothing to hierarchically organize.

rows.gap: Concurrent, background-style launch is described in skill text, but nothing in command.md confirms it's deliberately configured rather than just the tool's out-of-the-box behavior.
rows.fix: No action needed — default behavior already matches the doc's recommendation.

rows.gap: If a specialist's draft needs a second pass, current doctrine says rerun it fresh with the finding pasted under its brief [C22], not resume its own history — cheaper to write, more expensive in tokens than a true resume.
rows.fix: Try SendMessage-based resume the next time a specialist needs a correction pass, instead of a fresh relaunch, and compare token cost.

rows.gap: Nesting depth isn't config-capped, only convention-capped by the flat hub-and-spoke shape; a specialist that did try to spawn its own subagent wouldn't be technically blocked.
rows.fix: Not urgent given the doctrine already forbids peer/nested spawning by design [C15]; add the env var only if nesting is ever observed happening.

rows.gap: There's no config-level block on an unwanted agent type running; the only control is the main line choosing not to invoke it.
rows.fix: Not urgent — no unwanted-agent incident has been named; add a deny entry only if one turns up.

rows.gap: Every specialist runs at the same global effort regardless of how simple its job is (a PS fetch-and-extract likely doesn't need high effort), leaving cost on the table.
rows.fix: Set `effort: low` on PS (haiku, fetch/extract) roles specifically, since their jobs are narrow and mechanical by crew-grade design.

rows.gap: Commits happen every turn without fail, which is better-than-doc reliability, but the messages carry no information about what changed or why, and there's no PR step at all.
rows.fix: Have `_tools/autocommit.sh` append a one-line summary of the touched paths (already knows the file count) instead of just the count, without touching its "always exit 0" safety property.

rows.gap: This repo is mostly markdown/JSON/python utility scripts rather than a large typed codebase, so go-to-definition matters less, but there's still no tooling for it if a script layer grows.
rows.fix: Low priority; revisit only if the python tooling under `_tools/` grows large enough that grep stops being sufficient.

rows.gap: When a formation script errors (e.g. `check.py` or `assemble.py` failing), there's no stated habit of pasting the exact repro command — it likely happens ad hoc each time.
rows.fix: Adopt a one-line habit: paste the exact failing command plus its output when a formation script errors, before describing the symptom.

rows.gap: There is currently no path from a batch of autosave commits to a reviewable PR, even though the repo is public.
rows.fix: Only build this if a collaborator or review step is actually wanted; otherwise the local-commit model is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.

rows.gap: If a board or a design needed visual review (a screenshot of a published sit-rep page, say), there's no stated convention for handing Claude the image.
rows.fix: Adopt when a screenshot or asset actually needs review; no current convention exists to fall back on.

rows.gap: Nothing runs on its own cadence (a nightly digest refresh, a weekly RTB sweep); every run needs a live prompt from Chief.
rows.fix: Only worth building if a specific recurring need is named (e.g. a scheduled RTB sweep); no current pain point calls for it.

rows.gap: Same underlying gap as A19/E1/E2 — parallel sessions currently share one working tree with no filesystem-level collision guard.
rows.fix: See A19's fix: adopt `--worktree` for the second concurrent session.

rows.gap: Same root gap as A19/D18 — no isolated checkout exists for any parallel work.
rows.fix: See A19's fix.

rows.gap: Two live sessions editing the same files at once have no structural collision guard — only operator discipline (closing by session id) stands between them and a stomped edit.
rows.fix: Highest-value worktree fix of the three (E1-E3): give the second concurrent session its own `--worktree` so collisions become structurally impossible, not just avoided by habit.

rows.practice: Monitor parallel sessions from one screen
rows.gap: There's no single-screen view of what each concurrent session is doing; state has to be inferred from STATE.md/BOLO.md separately per session.
rows.fix: Try `claude agents` (or the Desktop app) the next time two sessions run at once, purely as a monitoring convenience — no restructuring required.

rows.gap: There is no short, project-scoped, checked-in file naming this repo's own conventions — everything either lives in the much larger SOP.md or in cross-conversation user memory that isn't project-specific.
rows.fix: Write a short root CLAUDE.md that points at SOP.md §1 and the skill list rather than duplicating either — same fix as A6.

rows.gap: Every rule in SOP.md applies everywhere by default; there's no way to scope a rule to, say, only the `_tools/bolostatus/` boards without it being one more paragraph in the same 57 KB file.
rows.fix: Only worth splitting out if SOP.md's size starts causing rules to be missed or ignored — not evidenced yet.

rows.gap: It isn't clear whether auto-memory's settings (what gets captured, how aggressively) have ever been reviewed or tuned versus just left at default.
rows.fix: Worth a one-time look at the auto-memory settings to confirm defaults match what's actually wanted, given how much the Command already leans on MEMORY.md.

rows.practice: CLAUDE.md treats context and enforcement differently
rows.gap: None of these rules are hook-enforced; per this read's own framing, that's not itself a problem to fix with a gate — the ruling for this BOLO is vocabulary first, no hook gates until a step is shown to actually get skipped, and this read found no step that is skipped, only steps enforced by habit rather than config.
rows.fix: No hook change now, per ruling 1; if a specific rule is later caught being skipped in practice, B2's PreToolUse hook is the cheapest place to add real enforcement for it.
